facts.text: MAE, MAPE and RMSE are standard metrics that summarize individual simulation-versus-measurement differences as one average error figure.
facts.quote: MAE, MAPE and RMSE are three standard ways to turn many individual simulation-versus-measurement differences into one average error figure.

facts.text: The booklet quotes a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.3 cm for a lidar survey method, meaning the model is typically about 1.3 cm off.
facts.quote: An MAE of 1.3 cm means the model is typically about 1.3 cm off; the booklet quotes that figure for a lidar survey method [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The booklet reports a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.7% on lidar signal amplitude for a clear-weather lidar model.
facts.quote: a 1.7% MAPE on lidar signal amplitude can sit beside an 8.5% MAPE on point count, the booklet's figures for a clear-weather lidar model [Chapters 6, 10].

facts.text: The booklet reports a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.5% on point count for a clear-weather lidar model.
facts.quote: an 8.5% MAPE on point count, the booklet's figures for a clear-weather lidar model [Chapters 6, 10].

facts.text: Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) misbehaves when measured values are near zero.
facts.quote: MAPE misbehaves when measured values are near zero.

facts.text: Large errors in a few simulation-versus-measurement comparisons are often what matters for a braking model.
facts.quote: whenever a few comparisons are badly wrong, which for a braking model is often what matters.

facts.text: MAE, MAPE and RMSE all hide the shape of simulation-versus-measurement errors.
facts.quote: All three hide the shape of the errors

facts.text: A radar validation paper noted that mean and RMSE errors cannot accommodate the random and knowledge-based uncertainty of stochastic detections.
facts.quote: a radar validation paper noted that mean and RMSE errors cannot accommodate the random and knowledge-based uncertainty of stochastic detections [Chapter 6].

facts.text: MAPE is used in published sensor-signal model evaluations as a reported metric rather than as a thresholded acceptance criterion.
facts.quote: MAPE is in published use for sensor-signal models, reported rather than thresholded

facts.text: Low average simulation error can coexist with dangerous optimism near the collision boundary.
facts.quote: low average error can coexist with dangerous optimism near the collision boundary.

facts.text: An average simulation error is only a starting point and is never sufficient for complete validation.
facts.quote: An average error is a start, never the whole validation [Chapter 10].
